subject: CardioMed — tenant purge manifest & signed attestation request
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@cardiomed.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T13:12:00Z
Subject: Per-tenant purge manifest + attestation request

Hi Priya,

Our legal team has requested a narrow-scope change for our dev and sandbox tenants: we want those non-prod tenant logs removed at 30 days while production remains at 90 days per our contract. They need an auditable proof-of-delete for the dev tenants that we can present to our internal auditors (SOC team) — specifically:

- A per-tenant deletion manifest listing object keys, timestamps, deletion job IDs and SHA256 checksums
- A signed attestation from Redwood stating the deletion jobs completed and no residual copies exist in hot storage
- Clarification on backups/replication windows and whether deletion is immediate across replicas

I'm attaching the scope-change that our counsel drafted. Can Redwood provide the manifest format and delivery options (API push, S3 drop, signed PDF)? Also please confirm whether there are any limitations (e.g. replication lag, snapshot retention) that would affect the effective deletion time.

Thanks,
Alex Moreno
Head of Security, CardioMed
security@cardiomed.com

Attachment: cardiomed-scope-change.pdf
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@cardiomed.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Per-tenant purge manifest + attestation request

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the scope doc. We can support a per-tenant purge path but need to align on the runbook and acceptable proofs. Quick summary of options from our side:

1) Programmatic purge + manifest: we run a tenant-scoped deletion job that emits a signed manifest (CSV/JSON) with object keys, deletion timestamps, job IDs and SHA256. We can deliver via secure S3 link or push to your ingestion API.

2) Snapshot-and-delete with attestation: we take a short-term snapshot for internal audit, then run purge and provide a signed attestation PDF and the underlying logs showing job execution. Snapshots are retained for a short forensic window (we'll confirm exact days).

3) Manual run + notarized DocuSign attestation: for legal/regulated asks we can provide a DocuSign-signed attestation template after the deletion job completes.

Questions for you: 1) Do you want an automated API push on job completion or a scheduled monthly manifest? 2) Which tenant IDs are in scope (please list dev/sandbox IDs)? 3) Any internal retention holds/e-discovery exceptions we should be aware of?

Olga, can you outline technical constraints (replication, backups, snapshots) and estimated lead time if we pursue option 1? Ben — I'll need Compliance to prepare the attestation template if CardioMed prefers DocuSign.

Next steps: once we have the tenant list and preferred delivery, we'll scope and give an ETA.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@cardiomed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Per-tenant purge manifest + attestation request — technical runbook

Hi all — technical notes and constraints from the serving/runtime side below. TL;DR: We can produce a per-tenant deletion manifest and a signed proof-of-delete, but there are replication and snapshot nuances to call out.

What we can deliver (option 1, programmatic purge):
- Deletion manifest schema (attached): row per object with fields: tenant_id, object_key, deletion_timestamp (ISO), deletion_job_id, storage_path, sha256_checksum, executor_node_id.
- A manifest signature: we will sign the manifest file with Redwood's compliance key and include a manifest-level SHA256 and timestamp.
- Push options: secure S3 drop (pre-auth link), SFTP, or API POST to a URL you provide.

Important operational constraints:
- Replication lag: objects are replicated across AZs; the deletion job marks objects deleted in metadata immediately but object physical GC can take up to 24 hours in cross-region replication scenarios. We will include GC completion timestamps in the manifest where applicable.
- Backups/snapshots: our automated daily snapshots are retained for 7 days in cold storage by default; a snapshot restore could reintroduce data if a long-term backup is later restored. If you require an irrevocable deletion path, we need to coordinate purge of snapshots/backups — that will be a separate process and may add 3–5 business days.
- For EU customers we maintain separate keystore rotation windows; not relevant here but I mention it for completeness.

Proposed timeline:
- Provide sample manifest schema and a test manifest: 2 business days
- Full implementation (API + signed manifest + attestation template): 7 business days after tenant list and confirmation on snapshot handling

Attachments: delete_manifest_schema.csv (CSV header + sample row)

If CardioMed wants the shorter 30-day retention to apply immediately to specified non-prod tenants, we'll need the explicit tenant IDs and written approval to also purge snapshots for those tenants (unless you accept the 7-day cold snapshot window).

Olga Petrov
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Attachment: delete_manifest_schema.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@cardiomed.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T18:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Per-tenant purge manifest + attestation request — compliance and next steps

Alex — thanks for raising this. From a Compliance perspective we can produce a signed attestation that references the deletion manifest and the execution logs. For legal acceptance we typically include:

- Statement of scope and tenant IDs
- Methodology (what was deleted, how manifests were generated, how signatures were created)
- Evidence bundle: deletion_manifest.csv, execution logs (redacted where necessary), and a DocuSign-signed attestation PDF

I've uploaded a draft attestation template to DocuSign; you can see it here: https://docusign.example.com/templates/ATT-9823. If CardioMed approves the language we will complete it when the deletion job finishes.

Proposed schedule:
1) CardioMed to send tenant IDs + confirm whether snapshots must be purged (Dec 2)
2) We produce a test manifest (Dec 4)
3) Production purge + signed attestation (Dec 9) — subject to confirmation on snapshot purge

If you want to accelerate beyond that we can run a prioritized job but may need an operational credit/expedite approval. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to finalize scope.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@cardiomed.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Per-tenant purge manifest + attestation request

Thanks, team. CardioMed confirms scope: two dev tenants (tenant_dev_42, tenant_sbx_17). We want the 30-day dev retention to be enforced immediately; we also request purging of the 7-day cold snapshot window for these two tenants as part of the scope. We approve the DocuSign template language as-is.

Please proceed with the prioritized path and the timeline you suggested (test manifest Dec 4, production purge + attestation Dec 9). We can take the test manifest via S3 link.

Also let's do a quick 20-minute sync tomorrow at 10am PT to confirm operational cutover.

Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Security, CardioMed
